segments.label: PAPER
segments.headline: Apple's robot, tested in real homes

beats.narration: You learned your way around a home by living in one. So can a robot that only practiced in computer-made homes handle a real one?
Apple researchers trained it only in homes built by a computer, then sent it into real homes it had never seen.
It sat on chairs, slipped through doors, and crawled under tables.
On simple tasks, it succeeded ninety-one percent of the time.

items.label: single tasks, in real homes it never saw

beats.narration: Why it matters, says the paper: this practice grows with computing power, not people's time.

visual.text: More computers, not more people's time
